features.description: A reviewed plan file exists for the Navidrome duplicate cleanup (D31): plan -> repoint -> trash as scripts/duplicate_cleanup.py, with the plan JSON schema, the hold rules, the reverse logs and the staged live runbook.
steps: Read docs/next-todos.md item 1, pivot spec D31, M9 spec section 3, docs/hard-won-facts.md, scripts/dedupe_copies.py, scripts/duplicate_report.py, crates/playlist_edit.py, crates/trash.py, sourcing/replace.py, and .harness/runs/dj-2026-10-17/progress.md (the initializer's entry fixes the defaults).

Write docs/plans/2026-10-17-n1-duplicate-cleanup.md in the style of docs/plans/2026-10-15-m3-dedupe.md: goal, facts (102 groups, 115 extra files, 59 extras in a playlist, 9 extras that are lossless beside a lossless keeper), design of `python -m scripts.duplicate_cleanup plan|repoint|trash`, the plan JSON schema ({"made_at", "groups": [{"keep": {id, path, suffix, bit_rate}, "extras": [{id, path, suffix, bit_rate, held_by: [playlist names]}], "hold": null | "both lossless" | "keeper missing on disk" | "keeper missing in Navidrome"}], "playlists": [{id, name, before, after}]}), the reverse logs (repoint-<ts>.jsonl with before/after per playlist, MOVES.txt for files), the lock rule (trash takes <dirname(CRATES_DB)>/worker.lock, so the worker must be stopped), the recompute-before-acting rule, and the task list N1-02..N1-05.

The plan names the safety tests each task must have: never trash while playlist_edit.references(db, extra) is non-empty (hidden rows included); refuse while a scan is running; a pair no longer in one duplicate_groups group is skipped; the keeper must exist on disk and not be missing in navidrome.db; every move has its MOVES.txt line before it happens.

Record the new defaults in docs/specs/2026-10-17-amperfy-pivot.md as new ledger rows `D35 *default*` (groups with two lossless copies are held, listed only, until Michael clears the hold in the plan JSON) and `D36 *default*` (the trash step runs only with the worker stopped, holding worker.lock, so beets has one writer), each in one sentence with what it replaces or refines.
Append a short entry to .harness/runs/dj-2026-10-17/progress.md (newest first) naming the plan file and the two defaults as direct questions for Michael.
Commit `N1-01: plan for the duplicate cleanup`.
.harness/check.sh is green

features.description: `python -m scripts.duplicate_cleanup plan` reads navidrome.db read-only, recomputes the duplicate groups, picks the keeper with scripts.duplicate_report.keep_rank, marks holds, lists which playlists (hidden rows included) hold each extra, and writes plan.json plus a markdown report without touching
steps: Test-first in tests/test_duplicate_cleanup.py against FakeSubsonicServer(db_path=...): add a `bit_rate` column to subsonic/fake_server.py NAVIDROME_SCHEMA and its media_file INSERT (from the song's `bitRate`), then a flac copy s9 of s3 'Move Your Body' (suffix flac, bitRate 900, duration 383, path 'Marshall Jefferson/The House Music Anthem/01 - Move Your Body.flac'); tests/test_fake_navidrome_db.py still passes.

scripts/duplicate_cleanup.py: `build_plan(navidrome_db, music_root) -> dict` uses scripts.duplicate_report.load + duplicate_groups (so the groups are recomputed from the live DB every time, never from docs/duplicates-report.md); keeper = group[0]; each extra lists `held_by` from crates.playlist_edit.references (hidden rows included) resolved to playlist names; `hold` is set to 'both lossless' when any extra's suffix is in duplicate_report.LOSSLESS beside a lossless keeper (D35), 'keeper missing on disk' when music_root/keep.path is not a file, 'keeper missing in Navidrome' when media_file.missing is set.

`playlists` in the plan: for every playlist holding an extra of an unheld group, before = navidrome.db playlist_tracks order, after = scripts.dedupe_copies.remap(before, {extra: keeper}) (an extra becomes the keeper in place; dropped when the keeper is already there).

`write_plan(plan, out_dir)` writes out_dir/plan.json and out_dir/report.md (sections: groups to act on with keeper and extras, held groups with the reason, playlists repointed before -> after counts); `--limit N` keeps the first N unheld groups; `--out` defaults to $CLEANUP_DIR or /data/duplicate-cleanup; the command prints the counts line.

Tests: s3+s9 form one group with keeper s9 and extra s3 held by 'Disco Edits' and 'Chicago 86'; pl-1 after == ['s1','s2','s9'] and pl-2 after == ['s9','s4','s5']; a hidden missing song in pl-1 still appears in held_by; two flac copies of one recording are held 'both lossless' and produce no playlists entry; a keeper whose file is absent under music_root is held; `--limit 1` with two unheld groups plans one; running plan twice writes identical JSON apart from made_at; nothing in navidrome.db, the fake's playlists or music_root changed (compare before/after).

Run .harness/check.sh tests/test_duplicate_cleanup.py tests/test_fake_navidrome_db.py tests/test_playlist_edit.py tests/test_duplicate_report.py while iterating; commit `N1-02: duplicate_cleanup plan`.
.harness/check.sh is green

features.description: `python -m scripts.duplicate_cleanup repoint --plan plan.json` repoints every playlist from each extra to its keeper through crates.playlist_edit.repoint_everywhere, after recomputing the groups, writing a reverse log line per edit, and starts a scan when done.
steps: Test-first in tests/test_duplicate_cleanup.py with the N1-02 fixture: `repoint(plan, client, navidrome_db, log_path, limit=None, dry_run=False) -> dict[str, str]` keyed by extra song id with values 'repointed N playlists', 'skipped: held (<why>)', 'skipped: no longer a duplicate of <keeper>', 'skipped: keeper missing', 'refused: <playlist>: <why>', 'dry run: would repoint <names>'.

Before acting on a group, recompute: duplicate_groups over the current navidrome.db must still put extra and keeper in one group and the keeper must not be missing; otherwise skip with the reason (the plan is advice, the live DB decides).

For each unheld extra call crates.playlist_edit.repoint_everywhere(client, db, extra, keeper); every value that is not 'repointed' (refused: owned by another user, PlaylistSkew on a hidden row, PlaylistChanged, failed) is reported and the command exits 1 at the end, but the other groups are still done. Smart playlists are 'skipped: smart playlist' as repoint_everywhere reports them.

Reverse log: before each repoint_everywhere call append one JSON line per affected playlist to log_path (repoint-<UTC timestamp>.jsonl beside the plan) with {ts, playlist_id, name, extra, keeper, before, after}; the after list is the one read back. `--dry-run` writes no log and sends no updatePlaylist (assert on srv.state.requests).
After the loop, when at least one playlist was repointed and not dry_run, call client.start_scan() once (the scan between repoint and trash).

Tests: the happy path repoints pl-1 and pl-2 to s9 and the log has two lines whose before equals the fixture order; a hidden missing song in pl-1 makes that playlist 'refused' with nothing written to pl-1 and pl-2 still repointed, exit code 1; a playlist edited after the plan is still repointed correctly because repoint_everywhere reads the current entries (the plan's before/after are advice only); a keeper deleted from the fake before repoint is 'skipped: keeper missing'; running repoint twice sends no second updatePlaylist; `--limit 1` acts on one group; a group held in the plan is never touched.
Commit `N1-03: duplicate_cleanup repoint`.
.harness/check.sh is green

features.description: `python -m scripts.duplicate_cleanup trash --plan plan.json` moves each extra to the trash with crates.trash.move_to_trash only when no playlist entry (hidden included) holds it, the keeper is on disk and listed, no scan is running and the worker lock is free; beets forgets it; everything is logged.
steps: Test-first: `trash(plan, client, navidrome_db, music_root, trash_root, lock_path, forget, log_path, limit=None, dry_run=False) -> dict[str, str]` with values 'moved to <trash path>', 'already gone', 'skipped: held (<why>)', 'skipped: no longer a duplicate of <keeper>', 'skipped: keeper missing', 'refused: still in <n> playlist entries', 'dry run: would move'.

Preconditions, each a test: raises WorkerRunning-style `CleanupRefused('stop the worker first')` when lock_path (<dirname(CRATES_DB)>/worker.lock) is held by another process (reuse sourcing.worker.hold_lock); raises CleanupRefused when client.scan_status()['scanning'] is true; an extra with any row in crates.playlist_edit.references(db, extra) is 'refused' and its file stays (a hidden missing row counts); the keeper must be a file under music_root and not missing in navidrome.db; the group is recomputed as in N1-03.

The move: crates.trash.move_to_trash(extra.path, music_root, trash_root) (its MOVES.txt line is written before the move; the test reads it back as `mv <quoted trash path> <quoted library path>`); then `forget(music_root / extra.path)` (sourcing.filer.BeetsFiler.forget in the worker; a failure is logged, not fatal); then one JSON line {ts, extra, path, keeper, trash_path} to trash-<UTC timestamp>.jsonl.
After the loop, when a file moved and not dry_run, client.start_scan() once. Exit 1 when anything was refused.

Tests (files under tmp_path/music created with real bytes): the happy path after N1-03's repoint moves s3's file to trash_root/<today>/<path>, MOVES.txt holds the reverse line, forget was called with the old absolute path, the plan's keeper file is untouched; before repoint the same call refuses with 'still in 2 playlist entries' and moves nothing; a hidden missing row in a third playlist alone blocks the move; a running scan refuses before any move; a held worker.lock refuses; `--dry-run` moves nothing and writes no log; a second run reports 'already gone' and does not call forget again; trash never overwrites (two runs on a restored file give a '(2)' name via free_path).
Commit `N1-04: duplicate_cleanup trash`.
.harness/check.sh is green
